threat_model_matrix.protected_asset: Individual transaction records and customer membership in bank training sets
threat_model_matrix.adversary: Curious federation coordinator, semi-honest participating banks, and external model query observers (membership inference / reconstruction attacks)
threat_model_matrix.guarantee: Bounded worst-case information leakage: P[M(D) in S] <= exp(epsilon) * P[M(D') in S] + delta for datasets D, D' differing by one training sample
threat_model_matrix.non_guarantee: Does not hide global population properties, aggregate fraud patterns, model architecture, or number of training rounds
threat_model_matrix.trust_assumption: Local client execution environment honestly executes gradient clipping and calibrated Gaussian noise injection before sending updates
threat_model_matrix.plaintext_boundary: Inside bank client local training process (pre-clipping and pre-noise gradients are visible only to client)
threat_model_matrix.key_owner: N/A (cryptographic keys not used; relies on entropy from secure random number generators)
threat_model_matrix.failure_semantics: Fails closed: invalid parameters raise ValueError; cumulative budget exhaustion raises PrivacyBudgetExceededError

threat_model_matrix.adversary: Curious aggregation server and passive network observers
threat_model_matrix.guarantee: The central server observes only the sum of client updates; individual client weights w_i are obscured by random zero-sum masks
threat_model_matrix.non_guarantee: Does not protect against collusion between the server and N-1 clients; does not protect against Byzantine poisoning or model reconstruction from the aggregate model itself
threat_model_matrix.trust_assumption: Clients follow the zero-sum masking agreement and masks cancel upon aggregation across honest participating clients
threat_model_matrix.plaintext_boundary: Client memory before masking; aggregate global model in server memory after summation
threat_model_matrix.key_owner: Clients negotiate or derive pairwise mask seeds
threat_model_matrix.failure_semantics: Gracefully bypasses masking when fewer than 2 participants are available; rejects malformed shapes

threat_model_matrix.protected_asset: Raw float model parameter vectors during server-side transport and aggregation
threat_model_matrix.adversary: Untrusted cloud aggregation coordinator and snooping network entities
threat_model_matrix.guarantee: Server computes weighted averages directly over polynomial ring ciphertexts without possessing the secret decryption key
threat_model_matrix.non_guarantee: Does not prevent client-side data poisoning; does not hide vector dimension or number of clients; subject to CKKS numerical precision bounds
threat_model_matrix.trust_assumption: Secret key remains isolated in client/consortium vault and is never transmitted to the aggregation server
threat_model_matrix.plaintext_boundary: Plaintext exists solely at client encryption and client/coordinator final decryption; server memory contains only CKKS ciphertexts
threat_model_matrix.failure_semantics: Fails closed: mismatched key IDs raise ValueError; corrupt ciphertexts fail decryption

threat_model_matrix.mechanism: Trusted Execution Environment (Intel SGX / AWS Nitro)
threat_model_matrix.protected_asset: Model parameters during plaintext aggregation in server memory
threat_model_matrix.adversary: Host operating system, hypervisor, cloud provider administrators, and privileged host processes
threat_model_matrix.guarantee: Memory encryption and cryptographic remote attestation (MRENCLAVE/MRSIGNER) guarantee execution of untampered code in isolated enclave
threat_model_matrix.non_guarantee: Does not protect against side-channel memory access timing attacks without cache mitigation; does not hide input/output communication volume
threat_model_matrix.trust_assumption: Intel / AWS hardware root of trust and uncompromised silicon microcode
threat_model_matrix.plaintext_boundary: Plaintext exists only within EPC (Enclave Page Cache) isolated memory pages; memory bus traffic is hardware-encrypted
threat_model_matrix.key_owner: Enclave hardware key derivation and attestation key pair
threat_model_matrix.failure_semantics: Truthfully labels software sandbox emulation vs physical SGX hardware; rejects tampered AEAD sealed data

threat_model_matrix.protected_asset: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) including customer account numbers, emails, phone numbers, and IBANs
threat_model_matrix.adversary: Cross-bank data leak observers, malicious auditors, and internal database operators
threat_model_matrix.guarantee: Deterministic 128-bit truncated HMAC tokens allow cross-bank entity resolution while preventing raw PII transmission or reversible identification
threat_model_matrix.non_guarantee: Does not provide information-theoretic anonymity against rainbow table attacks if HMAC secret key is compromised or input entropy is extremely low
threat_model_matrix.trust_assumption: Tenant-isolated KMS vaults securely store and protect HMAC secret keys per bank node
threat_model_matrix.plaintext_boundary: Raw PII is tokenized at the bank connector ingestion edge; only salted HMAC tokens enter shared intelligence networks
threat_model_matrix.failure_semantics: Fails closed on missing KMS key or malformed input

threat_model_matrix.protected_asset: Inter-bank and client-coordinator communication payloads and node identity
threat_model_matrix.adversary: Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) network interceptors, rogue client nodes, and DNS spoofing attackers
threat_model_matrix.guarantee: Bidirectional cryptographic identity authentication (X.509) and transport encryption enforcing CERT_REQUIRED and SAN validation
threat_model_matrix.non_guarantee: Does not protect endpoints against compromise once payload is decrypted in application memory
threat_model_matrix.trust_assumption: Root Certificate Authority (CFI-Root-CA / HashiCorp Vault PKI) private key integrity
threat_model_matrix.plaintext_boundary: Network wire is encrypted; plaintext exists in application memory after TLS socket decryption
threat_model_matrix.key_owner: Bank node leaf private key and Root CA
threat_model_matrix.failure_semantics: Connection abort on untrusted CA, expired certificate, SAN mismatch, or revoked serial in CRL
